hero.title: Six rules the work is held to.
hero.intro: Short enough to remember and strict enough to say no. Each one settles a tension that keeps coming back — and each comes with what it changes in practice.

states.low: All depth, no surface. Powerful, and hard to read.
states.mid: Depth held underneath, clarity on top.
states.high: All surface, no depth. Easy to read, and shallow.

states.low: Fast to ship, and has to be done twice.
states.mid: Quick iteration on foundations that last.
states.high: Built to last, but too slow to learn from.

states.low: Everything scoped. Safe, and nobody can do their work.
states.mid: Each role sees what concerns it.
states.high: Everything open. Convenient, and everyone sees everything.

aside.caption: Each principle below settles one of these tensions. Nothing here is measured or stored.

hero.title: The company behind the systems.
hero.intro: Hanoryx Systems designs and builds online systems, software platforms and the interfaces people use to work in them. Hanoryx North is its development team.

hero.title: Engineering, visible in the system.
hero.intro: This website is a working example: a scene registry, a shared animation scheduler, a quality budget and route-level code splitting. The panel on the right is live.

hero.title: Software systems, made visible.
hero.intro: We build online systems, platforms and interfaces. Explore the work, the systems behind it, and the team that builds them.

hero.title: Three ways to start work, and who decides when.
hero.intro: A clock, a pile of jobs, or something that happened: each of these can start the same piece of work, and each fails in its own way. This guide compares them on a burst of jobs you can resize, then sets out how to choose.

aside.caption: Three lanes, three kinds of starting gun.
Three lanes, three kinds of starting gun.

hero.title: The team behind the systems.
hero.intro: Hanoryx North is the development team behind Hanoryx Systems: platform architecture, interface systems, operational tooling and production-minded software engineering.

pillars.title: Platform architecture
pillars.body: Service boundaries, data models, and orchestration layers designed to carry operational load without ceremony.

pillars.title: Interface systems
pillars.body: Component systems and interaction models built as a controlled language, not a collection of screens.

pillars.title: Orchestration & automation
pillars.body: Internal tooling that removes manual operational drag and keeps multi-role coordination predictable.

pillars.title: Production-minded prototyping
pillars.body: Applied software engineering that ships fast, then hardens — foundations first, surface second.

hero.intro: Management layers, commerce infrastructure, automation, dashboards, data interfaces, client-facing portals and research — described as design areas, not as a count of deployed products.
